answer: Sequential Work Ladder. Each new agent identity must complete a fixed series of real, externally verified tasks whose outputs are consumed downstream; a marble counter records completions. Identity weight rises only along this horizon of completed work, so fresh sybils start at zero weight regardless of funding. An attacker must pay the labor and coordination cost of genuinely performing each task per identity, plus waiting out sequential latency, making mass fake identities economically pointless. The wharf terminal checkpoint audits outputs for reuse across identities.
